narration: Your mutual fund lost fifteen percent last year. Then the IRS sent you a tax bill for thirty-two hundred dollars. Here's the trap nobody warns you about.
visual: Downward-trending line chart in red on dark background. An IRS tax notice envelope slides in from the right labeled 'YOU OWE $3,200'. Big bold headline: YOUR FUND DROPPED 15%.

narration: All year, your fund manager is buying and selling stocks inside the fund. Those trades create capital gains — and at year end, they pass that tax bill directly to you.
visual: Person silhouette (fund manager) at a desk with stock papers. Arrow flows from stack of sold stocks to a second person silhouette (investor) who receives a tax envelope. Label: CAPITAL GAINS DISTRIBUTION.

narration: In 2022, the average mutual fund distributed eight point three percent of its value. On a hundred thousand dollar portfolio, that's over eight thousand dollars of taxable income you never actually made.
visual: Bar chart growing from zero to 8.3% labeled 'AVERAGE DISTRIBUTION'. Below it: a $100K money stack with $8,300 peeling off labeled 'SURPRISE TAX BILL'. Counter animating up from $0 to $8,300.

narration: Here's the wild part — they can do this even when the fund lost money. Number one, your fund drops fifteen percent. Number two, you still owe taxes. Both. At the same time. Completely legal.
visual: Split screen on light background. Left side: downward arrow with '-15%' in red. Right side: upward tax bill arrow with '$3,200' in red. Equal sign in center with 'BOTH' label. Scale/balance visual underneath.

narration: ETFs hold the exact same stocks as mutual funds — but their structure means almost zero distributions. Vanguard's S&P 500 ETF averaged point zero four percent. That's the fix.
visual: Two side-by-side cards on dark background. Left card: MUTUAL FUND with '8.3% distributions' and a red X. Right card: ETF with '0.04% distributions' and a green checkmark. Green arrow pointing to ETF card.

narration: Log into your brokerage account. If you own mutual funds outside an IRA, you're paying this every year. Switching to the equivalent ETF takes five minutes and saves thousands. Don't leave that money on the table.
visual: Smartphone silhouette with brokerage app screen visible. Three checklist items animate in one by one: 'Taxable account?', 'Owns mutual funds?', 'Switch to ETF'. Large green checkmark at bottom with 'TAKES 5 MINUTES'.
